notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 03/17/2025
Patient: Janyce Wintheiser, 70-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 03/17/2025. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 21.3 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 6% of all events. Oxygen saturation levels showed mild intermittent desaturation corresponding with apneic episodes. The overall findings are consistent with moderate sleep apnea. Clinical correlation and consideration of treatment options such as positive airway pressure therapy are advised. Follow-up assessment is recommended to evaluate treatment efficacy and symptom improvement.

Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 07/28/2026
Patient: Janyce Wintheiser, 71-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-related breathing disorder.

History:
The patient presents for follow-up regarding her sleep apnea treatment. She has been using CPAP therapy but reports difficulty tolerating the device.

Physical Examination:
BMI 25.2 kg/m2.

Assessment:
The patient's CPAP intolerance is confirmed by device download data. CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 2.2 hours per night on 26% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Plan:
Discuss alternative treatment options for sleep apnea, including oral appliance therapy and positional therapy. Continue to monitor symptoms and consider referral to dental sleep specialist if appropriate. Provide education on sleep hygiene and lifestyle modifications to improve sleep quality.

Follow-up:
Schedule follow-up appointment in 3 months to reassess symptoms and treatment adherence.
